Jetman and the Future of Human Flight

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
For Yves Rossy, his life is powered by one dream to fly like a bird..

Summary:
Jetman – The Future of Human Flight

“It’s a bird, it’s a plane, its Yves Rossy”

Yves Rossey aka Jetman is really only at home when he is soaring with his jet powered wings - 200 miles per hour - up into the sky, looking up into the clear blue skies…he is the superhero of the sky. Strapped to a jet-powered wing, — flying free, using his body as the rudder, soaring above the Swiss Alps or 8000 above the Grand Canyon.



Further information:
Swiss born Yves Rossy served as a fighter pilot in the Swiss Air Force where he flew fighter jets, but it was after experiencing the thrills of skydiving he discovered his passion for human winged flight. And set about exploring avenues to break the barriers of flying skin to air.
This resulted in his invention of the individual jet pack, which uses carbon fibre wings for flight. He has developed 15 different prototypes of the jet-pack, The current version, a 120 pound device has Rossy jumping out of an aircraft above 7,000 feet, free falling to gain speed and then soaring into the sky. Most of his flights last 15 minutes and cover up to 35 miles and include practicing complex maneuvers such as loops and flying in formation with airplanes. But the thrill is watching him fly. Wearing his single wing, Rossy really flies, steering with the movements of his body.
Sometimes things don’t work out as planned like an attempted crossing of the Strait of Gibralter…strong winds and clouds forced Rossy to ditch into the sea just three miles off the Spanish coast. He has crossed the English Channel, flown over the Swiss Alps and performed aerobatic loops around a hot-air balloon. In December He introduced his new protégé, famed 31 year old skydiver and BASE jumper Vince Reffet. Reffet is the second person in the world to earn the distinction of flying with the innovative Jetman wing. The adventurous duo also announced the completion of another first – a twin human formation flight over Dubai.
In December 2014, Yves Rossy also participated in an extraordinary formation flight over Dubai’s desert with Hungarian aerobatic champion Zoltan Veres. The pair’s record setting twin human formation saw them fly together over landmarks like the iconic Burj Khalifa, The Palm Jumeirah and the Liwa desert.

In his visit to South Africa we will get behind the story of Yves Rossy, why does risk his life and limb as he sets himself more and more daunting flying adventures, what inspires, what is his ultimate dream. Using the awe inspiring footage from his exploits his is a story that needs to be heard.

His is a life a life powered by one dream: to fly like a bird.

Press Release:


Jetman Defies Gravity
It’s a bird, it’s a plane... it’s Yves Rossy! Known as the Jetman, this Swiss military-trained pilot and aviation enthusiast is most at home strapped to his remarkable innovation - a single carbon fibre wing jetpack. Using his own body movements to perform astonishing aerobatic manoeuvres, he jets through the skies at over 300 kilometres per hour. Carte Blanche meets a superman defying gravity.


Script:


V/O
Wednesday morning, as the sun begins to rise in the outskirts of Dubai a Helicopter lands …..it’s pick up, a man known as Jetman who has spent the last 20 years perfecting what to most of us is Mission Impossible.

Yves: To be able to fly I wish everybody this emotion.
Yves: To to have that freedom so close to the dream to be a bird.

V/O
Yves Rossy, superhero of the sky…who with Jet powered carbon fibre wings of his own design takes to the skies reaching a speed of 300 kms an hour.

LINK: The wing is fixed, there is no rudder, ailerons or flaps, so Yves literally flies by the seat of his pants.

V/O
It's all in the way he moves his body.

Yves: With the speed the element air becomes consistent and like a very light water you can play with that
Derek: Just a small movement?
Yves: Very small, It’s the same you put your hand out of the window of the car you do like that Up, so we arch to go up you bend down goes down you twist a little bit your shoulder goes right and its very tiny.

V/O
56 year old, Swiss Born Yves used to fly fighter jets and commercial airliners

LINK: But it was skydiving that gave Yves the urge to fly like a bird of prey and he started experimenting with special wings more than 20 years ago

V/O
His mission to break the barriers of flying skin to air

Yves: in an airplane you are in a kind of a box and its fantastic you go and do aerobatics in the air but you are inside a box

V/O
In 2007 Yves flew across the English Channel in just 9 minutes, and an even bigger challenge was flying over the Swiss Alps, …..in every flight Yves improved his designs

Derek: You have developed many versions of the jet pack over the years?
Yves: About 15 different ones especially in the beginning you try things it was really learning by doing you cannot re invent the flight you copy birds and airplanes something in between.
LINK: Jet man is propelled by four tiny engines originally developed for model aircraft and they have to be perfectly synchronized.
Yves: 4 40 kg of thrust that means you have a big guy of 160 kilo that push you in the air you put that on a go cart you are better than a Formula 1 so its very powerful and that’s why also we can fly up to 60 degrees up steady, so its kind of a superman feeling when you have that push you have the power.

V/O
Things can and have gone wrong, but for Yves its always safety first.

Yves: If suddenly you are in an uncontrolled situation ok back to basics you release the wing and then again you are a normal sky diver so safety level is quiet high.
Derek: Always the reserve parachute
Yves: That is the plan B there is a parachute for the wing it comes slowly down and you have still 2 parachutes on your back. That’s why I am still here because we have that plan B.

V/O
Yves move to Dubai and the formation of Jetman Dubai has allowed him to, focus and expand his vision and build a team of innovative engineers and designers.

LINK: But reaching for the skies doesn’t happen amidst the skyscrapers of Dubai, this is jetman hq, situated in the desert about fifty kilometres from the city centre.

V/O
And coming on board is 31 year old Vince Refrett, champion sky diver and base jumper …Yves’s protégée.

Vince: I started to do my first flight without engine and Ya I was getting closer to this dream I was shaving since I’m 15 to fly like a bird. As sky diver you go down and the wing now we can stay on level and we can come up

V/O
Last Yves and Vince made history as together they jumped out of a helicopter and soared over the Skyline of Dubai

Yves: To be alone in the sky fantastic. I am flying but you don’t share that you fly in the air when you alone you see that you are doing a loop with your friend just beside you see also the outside, you see yourself flying almost.

V/O
For 10 heart stopping minutes this daring due performed what has been described as the first twin human formation over the city.

(VISUAL BREAK)

This week, we joined Vince on an early morning test flight…and here you see the team who back the pilot … equipment is checked and safety procedures ensured

And then its up to birdman

Vice zones in … opens his eyes and with a back flip he’s away.

Derek: What is your mental state?
Vince: full happiness, like the joy of going to fly its beautiful.
Derek: you caught us up very quickly… I was surprised because you went into quiet a dive.
Vince: I pick up speed looking at the helicopter on the side then when I get on level I slow down a little.

V/O
Depending on the thrust of the engine flying time is between 8 and 10 minutes using 28 litres of jetfuel

Derek: What amazed me is how relaxed you look flying next to us.
Vince: This wing or this machine it’s just an extension of my body, it’s beautiful.

V/O
Then like Cinderella the bird turns into a Sky diver as Vince opens the parachute and floats down to land

LINK: Then, just last year, the plans were drawn up for Yves most testing and adventurous flight. Flying along side the worlds biggest commercial airliner, the A 380

V/O
It took months to set up this project, to work out their flight plan, the turbulence around the airbus, the filming and convincing Emirates they were not crazy.

Yves: To have an A380 out of the line of operation from a company like emirates it’s not an easy thing you know these airplanes are meant to transport people not just to play.
Derek: Now as an ex pilot what was it like flying besides the worlds biggest commercial airline in the world
Yves: It’s a crazy machine, it did fly around 350 tons we are 160 kilos, this contrast it is magic…it is so gratifying when you have the impression its impossible and you do it….
Vince: it was so stable that it was easier than what we were expecting.
Yves: we were both of us on top of the rudder you have a A 380 in front of you like that and you fly in formation of that thing you have to pinch yourself to believe, fantastic.

V/O
Yves will be in South Africa this coming weekend, a guest at the Cape Argus Sports Show….

Yves: I am looking forward to discovering that beautiful region and the kind people.
Derek: No flight plan but I can see you heading over Table Mountain one day.
Yves: That will be good to be in the air almost naked like that it gives more substance to the region.

V/O 15 sec
Yves Rossy could sit back and look at his two decades of enormous achievement, of being at the fore front of discovery and development in pioneering human flight, but that’s just not his way

Yves: At the beginning I didn’t know why I did that its kind of a mission that was my destiny to come with the idea, thanks to the big bird.
Id like this art of flying continue I’m passing the baton to Vince.
